title: Introducing GildenSpire: Flight or Fight
description: Raise a dragon, take direct control in the sky, and discover what happens when flying becomes fighting.
imageAlt: A red GildenSpire dragon and rider flying toward a vast fantasy world as a rival approaches

body.heading: Considerably bigger wings
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive is building something with considerably bigger wings.
GildenSpire begins with a simple idea: raise a dragon, climb onto its back, and discover what happens when the world stops being something you walk through and becomes something you fly over.

body.heading: Flying is gameplay
paragraphs: Raising your dragon matters. Training matters. Discovering new dragons matters. But the heart of GildenSpire is what happens once you take off.

You will climb, dive, bank through mountain passes, cross enormous landscapes, discover places hidden from the ground, and eventually encounter other creatures that are not particularly interested in sharing the sky.
Then flying becomes fighting.
That is GildenSpire.
Flight or fight.
And we are only beginning to build the world.

title: Why Flying Has to Be Fun
description: The journey should be gameplay: direct flight, enormous terrain, curiosity, and combat that rewards control.
imageAlt: A rider directly controlling a red dragon over islands, castles, mountains, and waterfalls

body.heading: Getting somewhere should be part of the fun
paragraphs: There is a simple rule behind GildenSpire: getting somewhere should be part of the fun.
We do not want players to press a destination button and watch a dragon animation while the next screen loads.
We want you flying the dragon.

body.heading: Stay in the sky
paragraphs: We want mountains to feel enormous when you skim past them. We want diving toward an island to feel fast. We want you banking around towers, threading through ruins, climbing through clouds, and spotting something in the distance that makes you change direction just to see what it is.
And when combat begins, those same flying skills should matter.
A great dragon game should make you want to stay in the sky even when there is nowhere you are required to go.
That is one of the standards we are building GildenSpire around.

title: Building Dragons That Actually Feel Different
description: GildenSpire dragons are being designed as different creatures—not one model wearing different colors.
imageAlt: A collection of substantially different dragon species planned for GildenSpire

body.heading: Another dragon, not another skin
paragraphs: One red dragon, one blue dragon, one green dragon.
That is not enough.
GildenSpire is being designed around dragons that should actually feel different.
Different bodies. Different wings. Different movement. Different strengths. Different abilities. Different personalities.

body.heading: Different ways to fly and fight
paragraphs: A powerful fire dragon might feel heavy and aggressive in the air. A smaller air dragon might turn faster and climb differently. An ice dragon might completely change how a team approaches a fight.
The goal is not simply to collect another skin.
The goal is to discover another dragon.
And somewhere beyond all of them is the Golden Egg.

title: From Search to Opportunity: Building Whomly
description: How a search-first interface can turn public professional research into useful context and a thoughtful next step.
imageAlt: Whomly interface showing public professional search, profiles, AI-assisted context, and outreach preparation

body.heading: Start with the question
paragraphs: Whomly begins with the person you are trying to find: a general counsel in Chicago, a healthcare innovation leader, a potential board member, or a specialist whose public work fits the problem in front of you.
The search interface is being designed to accept useful professional criteria without turning research into an endless directory.

body.heading: Public research, organized
paragraphs: The hard part is rarely finding one more public page. It is understanding why a person may be relevant. Whomly is designed to organize publicly available professional information into readable context, saved people, and lists the user controls.

AI-assisted summaries and outreach drafts may help with the work, but the boundary matters: public professional context in, user-reviewed preparation out. No private-profile access, automatic contact, or release date is being claimed.

title: Welcome to BooYang City
description: A connected city gives us room for a zoo, bakery, boutique, school, hospital, and almost anything fun that might open next.
imageAlt: BooYang City artwork featuring a cheerful character and a colorful city of destinations

body.heading: A city is better than a menu
paragraphs: BooYang City is our framework for putting many different kinds of play inside one connected place. You look across the map, choose somewhere interesting, and enter a destination that has its own activity, characters, and progression.
The first destination ideas include the Zoo, Bakery, Boutique, School, and Hospital. Each should feel different, but every visit should make the larger city feel more alive.

body.heading: Begin with a tiny bakery
paragraphs: The Bakery captures the wider loop. Start small, learn recipes, serve customers, improve the kitchen, decorate the room, and gradually grow toward a café or restaurant. The place should visibly change because the player spent time there.
Opening a new destination should feel like opening a new toy box. BooYang City is in development, with no public build, platform, or release date announced.

title: Introducing Thumb Command: Save Planet Earth
description: Meet Blueguard and the worldwide arcade-defense campaign taking shape at Four of Hearts Interactive.
imageAlt: Blueguard interceptor defending Chicago from a purple alien invasion

body.heading: The city is the base
paragraphs: Thumb Command is a fast, colourful arcade-defense game in development around one clear mission: save Planet Earth.
Chicago, San Francisco, New York, London, and Tokyo establish the current campaign direction. No public build, store listing, or release date has been announced.

title: Making Sleep Data Feel Human
description: Sleep Readiness, Tonight’s Game Plan, Ask Amigo, Wind Down, and a small celestial companion give the numbers some warmth.
imageAlt: Sleep Amigo celestial companion and dark premium sleep guidance interface

body.heading: A score needs an explanation
paragraphs: A sleep score can be tidy and still leave a person wondering what to do next. Sleep Amigo is being built around that next question.
Sleep Readiness offers a quick assessment. Tonight’s Game Plan turns available information into a few things worth considering. Ask Amigo makes the experience a conversation instead of a spreadsheet.

body.heading: Sophisticated software can still have warmth
paragraphs: The new visual direction brings together midnight blues, aurora colour, clear glassy panels, and a small celestial Amigo who feels calm rather than clinical. Wind Down and Trends complete the current product idea.
Sleep Amigo remains in development. It is wellness software, not a medical device, and supported wearables or health sources will be named only after implementation is verified.

title: Building a Town That Refuses to Look Normal
description: Funky Town treats buildings as canvases and progression as a chance to make every neighborhood more expressive.
imageAlt: Funky Town artwork showing a bold neighborhood transformed by murals, color, music, and street art

body.heading: Buildings can become canvases
paragraphs: Many city builders begin with different intentions and slowly converge on the same neat grid. Funky Town begins with the opposite question: what if progress made the place stranger, louder, and more personal?
Murals, graffiti, sculpture, music, unusual architecture, parks, studios, cafés, rooftop gardens, and gathering places can give each district a different identity.

body.heading: Progress should change the view
paragraphs: The goal is not simply to make every building larger. It is to let players transform neighborhoods through creative decisions until two long-running Funky Towns could look dramatically different.
Community matters as much as colour. People and the places where they meet are what make the art feel alive. Funky Town is in development, with no public build or release date announced.

title: Building Unicorn Land Adventures
description: Unicorn creation, magical habitats, decorating, discovery, and mini-games define a distinct creative game.

body.heading: Current development direction
paragraphs: Unicorn Land begins with character creation and grows into habitats, gardens, discoveries, and mini-games.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

title: Inside Princess Land Adventures
description: Character style, castle rooms, cooking, decorating, and mini-games begin forming one creative game.

body.heading: Current development direction
paragraphs: Princess Land explores character styling, castle building, room decoration, cooking, and approachable mini-games.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

title: People Lens Is Becoming Whomly
description: The working name is retiring. Whomly better fits the journey from discovery to context to possible opportunity.
imageAlt: Whomly product identity and public-information people discovery interface

body.heading: A name that fits the whole idea
paragraphs: People Lens was a useful working name for a search concept. As the product grew toward profiles, context, lists, and outreach preparation, the name stopped describing the complete job.
The permanent product identity is Whomly. The old public route will keep forwarding here, but current navigation, metadata, product pages, and artwork now use the new name.

body.heading: Discover. Understand. Connect.
paragraphs: Whomly is about finding relevant people in publicly available professional sources, understanding why they may matter to a search, and organizing a possible next step.
That also means respecting the line between public research and private information. We are building the useful side of the line.

title: HeartStack Unicorn Blast Joins the Workbench
description: A first look at colourful combos, crystal cages, boosters, and unicorn rescue.
imageAlt: HeartStack Unicorn Blast colourful match board

body.heading: Current build direction
paragraphs: HeartStack combines colourful matching with cascading combos, boosters, crystal cages, and unicorn rescue sequences.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

title: Evil Doom Boy: Two Heroes, One Fight
description: Evil Doom Boy is one action-adventure game with Evil Doom Boy as the default hero and Evil Doom Girl as the alternate hero.
imageAlt: Evil Doom Boy and alternate playable hero Evil Doom Girl facing Evil Doom

body.heading: Choose who stands up to Evil Doom
paragraphs: Evil Doom is closing in. Begin as Evil Doom Boy or switch to Evil Doom Girl, then run, fight, swing, and survive long enough to stop it.
Evil Doom Boy is one game with two selectable heroes. The project remains in development; no public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

title: Bobby and the Breadstone
description: Bread-powered towers, branching paths, cheerful enemies, and one heroic dinosaur define Bobby’s direction.

body.heading: A small hero holds a very busy path
paragraphs: Bobby the Breadasaurus is a tower-defense adventure about placing bread-powered towers and protecting the Breadstone.
The project remains in development. No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

title: Why We’re Building Sleep Amigo
description: The harder sleep problem is not collecting another number. It is understanding what may matter tonight.
imageAlt: Sleep Amigo concept board with its celestial guide and nightly sleep interfaces

body.heading: A nightly conversation, not another dashboard
paragraphs: Sleep apps can produce a remarkable amount of data. The harder problem is deciding what deserves attention before bed.
We are building Sleep Amigo to help turn available sleep information into a simple nightly conversation: what may have mattered, what seems to be changing, and what is worth considering tonight.

body.heading: Why an Amigo?
paragraphs: The idea needs more warmth than a chart. A small celestial companion gives the product a voice without making the interface childish. The goal is premium sleep technology with someone friendly waiting inside it.
Sleep Amigo remains an in-development wellness concept. It does not diagnose conditions, replace professional advice, or claim unverified device compatibility.

title: The 4OH Card Table Adds Solitaire and War
description: Two familiar card games join Palace, Hearts, Spades, and Euchre in the Four of Hearts lineup.
imageAlt: Original Four of Hearts Solitaire card-table artwork

body.heading: More seats at the card table
paragraphs: Solitaire and War join the Four of Hearts card-table lineup as separate products with their own clear identities.
Both are in development. Neither has a public playable build or announced release date.

title: Palace 0.1.9 Enters Founder Review
description: The flagship card-table build advances through hands-on founder testing.
imageAlt: Palace castle artwork from Four of Hearts Interactive

body.heading: Testing the whole table journey
paragraphs: Founder review is focused on clarity, rules, accessibility, reconnect behaviour, and the journey from hand to hidden finale.
Palace remains an internal alpha. The website tutorial is a teaching preview, not a public production match.
